turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Hey, you got a sec? I need to vent about the migration last night.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? I saw the alert at 2 AM but figured it was routine.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Routine, my ass. I ran the schema migration in the maintenance window like we planned, but I skipped the backup step. I thought the tool would handle it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Wait, you didn't take a snapshot? You always take a full snapshot before touching prod.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I know, I know. And it bit me hard. The migration corrupted a bunch of customer records — addresses and phone numbers got scrambled.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's bad. But you had the old backups, right? You could restore from those.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Here's the kicker — the corruption spread to the backups too. Took me and the DBA team three days to repair everything. We're still verifying data integrity.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Three days? That's brutal. So what's the plan going forward?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I'm adopting a stricter policy — mandatory snapshot before any migration, and it also covers the deployment window. No exceptions, even for hotfixes.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Honestly, I'm surprised you didn't lock anything during the migration. That's the only silver lining.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yeah, no locks, but that didn't save me. Anyway, I'm scheduling all future deployments for off-peak hours, and I'll triple-check the backup chain.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pushed the new release this morning. Everything go smooth?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Smooth as silk. I took a full snapshot before, ran it in the maintenance window, and it finished without locking anything. No incidents.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Nice. So you're back on track after the disaster last week?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yeah, but I'm not taking chances. I've scheduled all deployments for off-peak hours now — no more peak-hour releases. That's what caused the outage last time, remember?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Right, the outage. That was a mess. But at least you've got a system now.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Exactly. And I've got a checklist that includes the backup verification step. I'm not touching prod without it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, congrats on the last three releases — all green, no incidents. That's a streak.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Thanks. It feels good. I've been sticking to the new policy — snapshot before, off-peak window, and I even added a rollback test.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So the stricter policy is working? The one that covers the deployment window too?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yeah, that's the key. I used to think maintenance windows were enough, but after the corruption fiasco, I realized the whole process needed guardrails.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Well, you've definitely turned it around. No more 3 AM panic calls.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Fingers crossed. But I'm still paranoid about backups — I check the snapshot integrity before every single migration now.
